step1_figure.circuit_type: Wide-swing (rail-to-rail input) folded-cascode op-amp with class AB output buffer
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.48 illustrates a wide-swing operational amplifier featuring complementary NMOS and PMOS differential input pairs, a folded-cascode stage with floating current-source biasing, and a push-pull class AB output stage (MOP/MON) compensated by a 240 fF Miller capacitor to drive heavy resistive and capacitive loads (1 kΩ || 10 pF).

equation.formula: A_OLDC = (g_mn + g_mp) * (R_ocasn || R_ocasp) * (g_mp_out + g_mn_out) * (r_on_out || r_op_out || R_L)
equation.explanation: Product of the input differential stage transconductance, the folded-cascode stage output resistance, the push-pull output stage transconductance, and the total output load resistance.
equation.assumptions: Both NMOS and PMOS input pairs are active in mid-supply common-mode bias; output stage operates in class AB.

sky130_expected.calculation: With I_tail = 20 uA (10 uA per branch), g_mn ≈ sqrt(2 * 270u * 50 * 10u) = 520 uS, g_mp ≈ sqrt(2 * 50u * 100 * 10u) = 316 uS, total g_m1 ≈ 836 uS. Cascode stage resistance R_out1 ≈ (g_m_cas * r_o^2) / 2 ≈ 0.5m * (1M)^2 / 2 ≈ 250 MOhm (practically ~20-50 MOhm with short-channel effects). First stage gain Av1 ≈ 836 uS * 20 MOhm ≈ 1.67e4 (84 dB). Output stage with R_L = 1 kOhm has gain Av2 ≈ g_m2 * R_L ≈ 10 mS * 1 kOhm ≈ 10 (20 dB). Under heavy resistive loading (1 kOhm) and short-channel ro degradation, overall gain is approximately 50 to 65 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Channel length modulation and resistive load of 1 kOhm lower the DC gain compared to an unloaded OTA.

equation.explanation: Unity-gain frequency set by the combined transconductance of the complementary input pairs and the Miller compensation capacitance Cc.
equation.assumptions: Both input differential pairs are conducting around VDD/2; Cc = 240 fF.

sky130_expected.calculation: g_m1 = g_mn + g_mp ≈ 520 uS + 316 uS = 836 uS. With Cc = 240 fF: f_un = 836e-6 / (2 * pi * 240e-15) ≈ 554 MHz. Parasitics reduce this to approximately 300 - 500 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Text page 806/807 notes fun approaches 400 MHz when using short channel lengths.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin at the unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Phase difference from -180 degrees at the unity-gain frequency under Cload = 10 pF and Rload = 1 kOhm.
equation.assumptions: Miller compensation dominant pole approximation with output pole pushing.

sky130_expected.calculation: Due to heavy capacitive load (10 pF) and moderate Cc (240 fF), the non-dominant pole moves inward, yielding a phase margin typically between 45 and 65 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Fig. 24.38 and Fig. 24.45 show phase margins around 45° to 60° when driving pF loads.

slew_rate_rising.description: Positive output slew rate when driving 10 pF load

equation.explanation: Rate of change of output voltage when charging the load capacitor via MOP in class AB mode.
equation.assumptions: Output device MOP provides peak current exceeding quiescent bias.

sky130_expected.calculation: From Fig. 24.49, output steps from 100 mV to 900 mV in roughly 5 ns across 10 pF. SR ≈ 0.8 V / 5 ns = 160 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Large output PMOS (1000/1) delivers several milliamperes during large-signal transients.

slew_rate_falling.description: Negative output slew rate when discharging 10 pF load

equation.explanation: Rate of change of output voltage when discharging the load capacitor via MON.
equation.assumptions: Output device MON is fully turned on.

sky130_expected.calculation: Falling edge from 900 mV to 100 mV in ~5 ns with 10 pF load: SR- ≈ 0.8 V / 5 ns = 160 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Large output NMOS (500/1) rapidly sinks load current.

settling_time.description: Settling time to 2% for 100 mV to 900 mV input step

equation.explanation: Combined slew time and small-signal settling in unity gain follower configuration.
equation.assumptions: Follower configuration (beta = 1) driving 1 kOhm and 10 pF.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text on page 804 states settling time is approximately 5 ns for L=1 devices. With 10 pF load in Fig 24.49, settling is between 5 ns and 15 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Figure 24.49 transient simulation displays settling within 10 ns.

input_common_mode_range.description: Valid input common-mode voltage range with operational differential pair

equation.explanation: Dual complementary input pairs enable operation across the entire supply range from ground to VDD.
equation.assumptions: NMOS operates near VDD, PMOS operates near GND, both operate in middle.

sky130_expected.calculation: At VDD = 1.8V, PMOS pair operates from 0V to ~1.2V, NMOS pair operates from ~0.6V to 1.8V, covering 0V to 1.8V completely.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Rail-to-rail input topology ensures functionality from rail to rail.

quiescent_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD under equilibrium

equation.explanation: Sum of all branch currents under zero differential input.
equation.assumptions: Bias circuit supplies ~140 uA, core OTA branches draw ~10-20 uA each, output stage draws quiescent class AB current.

sky130_expected.calculation: Bias generator: ~140 uA. OTA stages: 6 branches * 10 uA = 60 uA. Output stage class AB quiescent current: ~100-300 uA. Total current: ~300 uA - 600 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Text specifies bias circuit consumes 140 uA, and total supply current is shown around 300 to 500 uA.

step3_testbench.description: SPICE testbench for Fig. 24.48 rail-to-rail op-amp measuring DC operating point, open-loop AC response (gain, GBW, PM), and closed-loop transient response (follower driving 1k || 10pF step from 100 mV to 900 mV).
